subject: POC success criteria & KPIs — Atlas Payments
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Sofia Ramos <sofia.ramos@atlas-payments.com>, Carlos Mendez <carlos.m@atlas-payments.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-07-20T15:02:00Z
Subject: POC success criteria & KPIs — Atlas Payments

Hi Sofia / Carlos —

Great to meet earlier today. Per our discovery, I wanted to recap the agreed POC goals and propose measurable KPIs so we can finalize the evaluation plan and timeline. Attaching a worksheet with the fields below for your review.

Summary of objectives (what success looks like):
- Integrate Redwood inference into Atlas Payments’ customer support pipeline to generate categorized suggested replies and automate simple claim triage.
- Validate latency/throughput and cost under realistic peak traffic patterns.
- Ensure output quality meets your manual-review pass rate threshold.

Proposed KPIs (measurable targets):
1) Latency: P50 < 200ms, P95 < 800ms for 512-token requests (target environment: g4dn-equivalent)
2) Throughput: sustain 60 concurrent sessions with steady-state request rate of ~8 req/s per session (target aggregate ~480 req/s) with <5% error rate
3) Cost: target average cost/token <= $0.0009 (token accounting measured via Redwood usage logs)
4) Quality: 85% acceptance rate on sampled set of 500 end-to-end replies (human reviewer pass), and no critical hallucination incidents during trial

POC plan & ownership (proposed):
- Eng onboarding & infra: Dylan (Redwood) — environment, sample dataset ingest, baseline perf runs
- Success criteria & QA: Marissa (Redwood) & Sofia (Atlas) — define review rubric and sampling cadence
- Program lead / escalation: Jordan (Redwood) — weekly check-ins, blockers, and scope changes

Proposed timeline:
- Week 0 (this week): finalize success criteria and access (API keys, sample data)
- Week 1: infra/setup + baseline perf tests
- Week 2: run steady-state traffic, collect metrics, and sampling for quality review
- Week 3: consolidation, final report, and decision meeting

Next steps (please reply with confirmations / edits):
- Confirm the KPI targets above (especially latency and quality thresholds)
- Share list of sample conversations and any PII redaction rules
- Confirm kickoff for Week 1 (suggest Mon 2027-07-26)

Attachments: Atlas-POC-success-criteria-20270720.xlsx (spreadsheet) — includes measurement plan and rubric

Thanks —
Jordan Blake
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

From: Sofia Ramos <sofia.ramos@atlas-payments.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Carlos Mendez <carlos.m@atlas-payments.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-07-21T09:18:00Z
Subject: Re: POC success criteria & KPIs — Atlas Payments

Jordan — thanks for the thorough recap. Quick notes / clarifications from our side: 

- Overall this looks good. A few items to tighten:
  * Latency: can we aim for P95 <= 600ms? Our UX team is stricter on tail latency for customer-facing suggestions. If that requires a model variant or aggressive batching controls, call that out so we can scope tradeoffs.
  * Throughput: 480 req/s sounds right for peak but typical will be ~120 req/s — we want to see behavior under both burst and steady.
  * Cost: the $0.0009/token is an aspirational target — please include a sensitivity table for cost at varying batching and quantization settings.
  * Quality: we want to be explicit about what 'critical hallucination' means — proposing: any answer that includes a fabricated transaction ID or incorrect legal/regulatory statement counts as critical.

- Access: we can provide a sampled dataset (2k anonymized support transcripts) by EOD Fri 2027-07-23; our security team requires that all PII be hashed prior to upload. Dylan — can you confirm Redwood’s controlled ingest path and whether we need an IP allowlist?

- Timeline: Week 1 kickoff on Mon 2027-07-26 works for us. We’d like a 30-min kickoff to align on test harness and data schema.

Thanks,
Sofia
Head of Product — Support Automation
Atlas Payments

Thanks — good calls out. Short responses inline and updated asks below.

- Latency: we can update target to P95 <= 600ms for the customer-facing suggestion use case. To hit that consistently we'll propose a compatible model variant and a conservative batching policy (max batch latency 30ms). I'll include two configurations in the attachment: "balanced" (meets 600ms P95) and "cost-optimized" (P95 ~800ms but lower cost/token).
- Throughput: we'll run two phases — steady-state (120 req/s) and burst (480 req/s) — and deliver separate reports.
- Cost: included sensitivity table in the attached PDF (POC-eval-plan-Atlas-20270720.pdf).
- Quality: agreed on your definition for critical hallucination. We'll include the rubric in the spreadsheet and sample checklists for the 500-review sample.

Security / ingest: Dylan — can you confirm the ingest path and whether we need an IP allowlist? Dylan?
